title: Koszul powers detect supported objects on an affine scheme
statement: Let X=Spec(A) be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f_1, ..., f_r be elements of A, and let U=X minus V(f_1, ..., f_r). For each tuple e=(e_1, ..., e_r) of positive integers, let K_e be the bounded Koszul complex on f_1^{e_1}, ..., f_r^{e_r}, regarded as a perfect object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. If E is in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and E restricted to U is zero, then E=0 whenever Hom(K_e[n],E)=0 for every tuple e and every integer n.

proof.text: For each integer n and morphism φ:O_X[n]→E, apply lem-pc-koszul-supported-augmentation-vanishing to obtain an index e with u_e[n] followed by φ equal to zero. This step needs only the restriction-zero hypothesis, not orthogonality.

source.place: Tag 09IR, proof using Lemma 36.9.6 and Lemma 36.3.5

proof.text: Extract the Koszul triangle I_e→O_X→K_e from lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology, applying that theorem in standard localizations and transporting the triangle along the canonical triangulated localization equivalence. Shift the triangle by n. Yoneda exactness factors φ through K_e[n]. The diagonal tuple of positive exponents e+1 in horth makes the factor zero, hence φ=0. A termwise identity natural isomorphism between koszulOpenTilde and Mathlib tilde identifies K_e with the hypothesis object. Triangle shifting multiplies arrows by (-1)^n; this unit preserves the zero-precomposition equality.

proof.text: ExtendSingleIso, singleMapHomologicalComplex and tildeSelf identify the structure object with the derived single structure sheaf. All its shifted Hom sets into E are now subsingletons. Apply the zero-detection clause of lem-pc-perfect-generation-affine-base in a standard localization to a representative complex of E, whose quasi-coherent cohomology is transported by homologyFunctorFactors. Transfer the single-source Hom sets through Localization.homEquiv and transport zero back through Localization.uniq. This is precisely the affine derived-equivalence argument of the original plan, using its existing generator-criterion corollary.

lean.statement: theorem isZero_of_koszul_powers_orthogonal (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace))] (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) (hU : U = ⨆ i : Fin r, PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f i)) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace).over U))] (E : schemeDerivedQCohCategory (Spec (.of A))) (hres : IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E.obj)) (horth : ∀ (e : Fin r → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < e i) → ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (((DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ (ModuleCat.{u} A) (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _ (tilde.functor (.of A)) ⟨fun _ _ ↦ tilde.map_zero⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ f i ^ e i)).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)))⟦n⟧) ⟶ E.obj)) : IsZero E.obj
lean.note: Uses the landed Koszul complex, extended to nonpositive cochain degrees and sheafified termwise with Mathlib tilde. Explicit zero-map preservation is Mathlib tilde.map_zero; it selects the shared sheaf-module category without introducing another derived-category instance.
